[[Russell 2000 Index]] component | hq_location_city = [[Dallas, Texas]] | hq_location_country = US | website = {{URL|https://nl-ind.com}} }} '''NL Industries''' ({{NYSE|NL}}), formerly known as the '''National Lead Company''', is a lead smelting company currently based in [[Dallas, Texas]]. National Lead was one of the 12 original stocks included in the [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] at the time of its creation on May 26, 1896.{{cite web |url=http://www.fool.com/Features/1996/sp0529a.htm |title= History of the Dow |publisher=[[The Motley Fool]] |date=1996-05-29 |archive-date= 2006-06-12 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20060612210702/http://www.fool.com/Features/1996/sp0529a.htm |url-status=dead}} [[File:NL Industries (Dutch Boy Paint) Specimen Stock Certificate, c.1975.jpg|thumb|NL Industries (Dutch Boy Paint) Specimen Stock Certificate, c. 1975]] ==History== It began business in [[Philadelphia]] in 1772. The name "National Lead Company" was used since 1891 after a series of mergers. National Lead changed its name to NL Industries in 1971.{{cite web |url=http://www.library.hbs.edu/hc/lehman/chrono.html?company=national_lead_company |title=National Lead Company |access-date=2011-10-24 |publisher=[[Harvard University]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100630012155/http://www.library.hbs.edu/hc/lehman/chrono.html?company=national_lead_company |archive-date=2010-06-30}} ===California lead paint liability case=== NL Industries has encountered legal problems based on their long history of selling [[lead paint]]. Exposure to lead paint can cause numerous health and developmental problems in children and adults, and its use has been banned or restricted in many countries. In January 2014, the [[Santa Clara County Superior Court]] ruled that NL Industries, along with [[Sherwin-Williams]] and [[ConAgra Foods|ConAgra]], were [[Joint and several liability|jointly and severally]] liable for $1.15 billion, to be paid into a lead paint abatement fund to be used to remove lead paint from older housing.{{cite news |last1=Rosenblatt |first1=Joel |date=2013-12-17 |title=Sherwin, NL, ConAgra Lose $1.1 Billion Lead Paint Ruling |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2013-12-16/sherwin-nl-conagra-lose-1-1-billion-lead-paint-verdict-1-.html |newspaper=Bloomberg News |accessdate=2014-11-25}}{{cite news |last=Rosenblatt |first=Joel |date=2014-01-08 |title=Manufacturers Must Pay $1.15 Billion in Lead Paint Suit |url=http://www.businessweek.com/news/2014-01-07/manufacturers-must-pay-1-dot-15-billion-in-lead-paint-lawsuit-1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111055809/http://www.businessweek.com/news/2014-01-07/manufacturers-must-pay-1-dot-15-billion-in-lead-paint-lawsuit-1 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 11, 2014 |newspaper=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]] |accessdate=2014-11-25}} The judge ruled that the paint companies manufactured, marketed, and sold lead paint without disclosing the health risks to the consumers in spite of "actual and constructive knowledge that it was harmful".{{cite news |last=Elias |first=Paul |date=2013-12-17 |title=Lead Paint Lawsuit: Judge Orders 3 Companies To Pay $1.1 Billion For Removal Services |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/12/17/lead-paint-lawsuit_n_4458145.html |newspaper=[[Huffington Post]]|accessdate=2014-11-25}}{{cite web |url=http://www.scefiling.org/filingdocs/194/69616/endorse_109122_StatementxofxDecisionxFINAL.pdf |title=Judge Kleinberg's Order, final statement of decision, Case Number 1-00-CV-788657 |last1=Kleinberg |first1=James |date=7 January 2014 |website=Santa Clara County Superior Court's Electronic Filing System. |accessdate=26 August 2014 |quote="The defendants sold lead paint with actual and constructive knowledge that it was harmful" |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407042633/http://www.scefiling.org/filingdocs/194/69616/endorse_109122_StatementxofxDecisionxFINAL.pdf |archive-date=7 April 2014 |url-status=dead }} The disposition of ''The People v. ConAgra Grocery Products Company et al.'' in the California 6th Appellate District Court on November 14, 2017, is that: {{blockquote|... the judgment is reversed, and the matter is remanded to the trial court with directions to (1) recalculate the amount of the abatement fund to limit it to the amount necessary to cover the cost of remediating pre-1951 homes, and (2) hold an evidentiary hearing regarding the appointment of a suitable receiver. The Plaintiff shall recover its costs on appeal.{{cite web |url=http://appellatecases.courtinfo.ca.gov/search/case/mainCaseScreen.cfm?dist=6&doc_id=2073589&doc_no=H040880&request_token=NiIwLSInLkg%2BWyApSSFdUExJUEg7UCxbJyJeJzJTMCAgCg%3D%3D |title=The People v. ConAgra Grocery Products Company et al. |author1=Judge Nathan D. Mihara |author2=Associate Justice Eugene M. Premo |author3=Associate Justice Franklin D. Elia |date=2017-11-14 |website=California Courts - Appellate Court Case Information |publisher=Judicial Council of California |access-date=2017-11-19 |quote= ... we can accept the inference that defendants' pre-1951 promotions increased the use of lead paint on residential interiors during the period of those promotions ...}}}} On February 14, 2018, the California Supreme Court denied the defendants' request for review, sending the case back to the trial court as ordered by the Appellate Court.{{cite web |url=https://appellatecases.courtinfo.ca.gov/search/case/dockets.cfm?dist=0&doc_id=2239732&doc_no=S246102&request_token=NiIwLSIkXkw9WyBVSCNNSE1IUFg0UDxTJyM%2BQzpTUCAgCg%3D%3D |access-date=2024-08-24 |title=PEOPLE v. CONAGRA GROCERY PRODUCTS COMPANY Division SF Case Number S246102}} NL Industries settled its part of the suit in May, 2018 with a payment of $60 million and a pledge to stop supporting the ConAgra and Sherwin-Williams backed ballot measure proposed for the November, 2018 ballot {{cite news |last1=Dillon |first1=Liam|date=2018-06-26 |title=Will paint companies pay to clean up lead in homes? California voters could decide in November |url=http://www.latimes.com/politics/la-pol-ca-lead-paint-initiative-qualifies-20180626-story.html |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |accessdate=2018-06-26}} ===National Lead and Dutch Boy Paints=== In 1907, National Lead entered the consumer market for titanium paints, creating a product line under the name "[[Dutch Boy Paint|Dutch Boy]]". Dutch Boy paints competed with other brands that contained mineral products supplied by National Lead. The "Dutch Boy Painter", which was created by [[Lawrence Carmichael Earle]], became National Lead's symbol for many years. NL Industries sold off the Dutch Boy brand in 1980 to [[Sherwin-Williams]], two years after the [[U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission|CPSC]]'s directive banning the manufacturing of lead housepaint went into effect. ==CompX International== {{Infobox company | name = CompX International Inc. | logo = | type = [[Public limited company]] | traded_as = {{NYSE MKT|CIX}}{{Citation|url=http://compx.com/corp-info.html|title=traded marks}}
[[Russell 2000 Index]] component | founded = August 4, 1993 | hq_location = [[Dallas]], [[Texas]] | area_served = [[the United States]] | key_people = David Bowers
(CEO) | industry = [[Security]] & Protection Services | services = Security Products, Furniture Components and Marine Components | operating_income = {{profit}} US$ {{0|0}}83.2 million (2012){{Citation|url=http://yahoo.brand.edgar-online.com/displayfilinginfo.aspx?FilingID=9141967-41923-46732&type=sect&dcn=0001193125-13-094118|title=2012 Annual Report}} | net_income = {{profit}} US$ {{0|0}}35.0 million (2012) | assets = {{profit}} US$ {{0|0}}150.2 million (2012) | equity = {{profit}} US$ {{0|0}}102.1 million (2012) | num_employees = 466 (2013){{Citation|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/q/pr?s=CIX|title=number of employees}} | website = {{URL|http://www.compx.com}} }} '''CompX International Inc.''' is one of the largest manufacturers of security products and recreational marine components in the world.{{cite web|url=http://media.corporate-ir.net/media_files/IROL/11/116425/CIX_Annual_Report_2012_Final.pdf|title=General business in annual report}} Located in [[Dallas]], [[Texas]], CompX International Inc. is also a subsidiary of NL Industries, Inc. The business of the company is divided into three segments: Security Products, Furniture Components and Marine Components. Their products are designed to meet the high-end applications.{{cite web |url=http://compx.com/corp-info.html |title=Corporate Profile - CompX International Inc. (NYSE MKT:CIX) |author= |date=n.d. |website=CompX |publisher=self published |access-date=January 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130703150912/http://compx.com/corp-info.html | archive-date=2013-07-03}} CompX International Inc. offers its products through original equipment manufacturers and distributors.{{Citation|url=http://compx.com/corp-info.html|title=Company descriptions}} ===History=== Based in [[Dallas]], [[Texas]], CompX was founded to open business on August 4, 1993.{{Cite web|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/q/pr?s=CIX|title=Foundation in Yahoo|accessdate=19 June 2025}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/finance/stocks/companyProfile?symbol=CIX|title=foundation time|website=www.reuters.com|accessdate=19 June 2025}}{{better source needed |date=January 2022}} In March 1998, CompX International Inc. completed its [[initial public offering]], making it a [[public company]] with stocks traded on the [[New York Stock Exchange]] under the symbol of '''CIX'''. In 1999, CompX International moved the corporate headquarters from [[Mauldin, South Carolina|Mauldin]], South Carolina, to [[Houston]].[http://www.bizjournals.com/houston/stories/1999/01/11/daily3.html "CompX moves to Houston" Houston Business Journal]{{Cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1876&dat=19990112&id=KUEfAAAAIBAJ&sjid=wc8EAAAAIBAJ&pg=4968,3229380|title=Herald-Journal - Google News Archive Search|website=news.google.com|accessdate=19 June 2025}} On Jan 11, 2000, CompX International Inc. acquired Chicago Lock Co. successfully for about $9.2 million in cash, which was borrowed under its existing credit facility.{{cite web| url = http://www.bizjournals.com/houston/stories/2000/01/10/daily5.html| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20060210150811/http://www.bizjournals.com/houston/stories/2000/01/10/daily5.html| archive-date = 2006-02-10| title = CompX International completes acquisition of Chicago Lock - 2000-01-11}} In May 2002, CompX International achieved an agreement to close its Dallas corporate office.[http://www.bizjournals.com/dallas/stories/2002/08/26/story4.html CompX International close Dallas corporate office] In September 2004, NL Industries completed the acquisition of 68% of CompX International for $168.6 million.{{cite web|url=http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nl-industries-closes-buy-of-68-of-compx-for-1686m |title= NL Industries closes buy of 68% of CompX for $168.6M |date=September 24, 2004 |accessdate=Dec 6, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090720042541/https://www.marketwatch.com/story/nl-industries-closes-buy-of-68-of-compx-for-1686m |archive-date=2009-07-20}} In December 2012, CompX International Inc. sold its Furniture Components operations to Knape & Vogt Manufacturing Company for approximately $59 million in cash.{{cite web |url=http://www.marketwatch.com/story/compx-announces-the-completion-of-the-sale-of-its-furniture-components-operations-2012-12-28|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131205104625/http://www.marketwatch.com/story/compx-announces-the-completion-of-the-sale-of-its-furniture-components-operations-2012-12-28|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 5, 2013|title=COMPX Announces the Completion of the Sale of its Furniture Components Operation}} ===Leadership=== The main officers of the company are listed as follows:{{Cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/finance/stocks/companyOfficers?symbol=CIX|title=Managers|website=www.reuters.com|accessdate=19 June 2025}} *David Bowers -
